analysis: The only changed file is docs/architecture/inference.md, with one documentation-only hunk (head lines 1116-1128). It describes Qwen inline MTP assistant behavior: chained ordinary decode with hidden-row history, a carry stored once no successor is in flight, per-drafter opt-in via supportsOrdinaryDecodeHistory, and the rollback env switches DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CHAINED and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CARRY. The supplied units are the base text (lines 1619-1764, outside the changed range) and head text (lines 1-415), so the changed hunk itself is visible only in the patch excerpt and not in a numbered unit. No code, key, protocol, attestation, authorization or cache-storage change is in this PR's supplied scope. The prose adds no new attack surface, and no control is weakened or removed. The threat model's T-041 and TB-007 concerns (cross-tenant prefix cache, SSD tier, TTL) are not modified by the described text. The MTP history/carry is in-process engine state, not persisted. The underlying code in EngineLoopV2+MTPOrdinaryHistory.swift is not supplied. Whether chained history or carry state could leak across requests or tenants, or interact with SSD prefix-cache checkpoints (the CBv2MTPPrefixCheckpointCoding contract), is unverified and belongs to review of the code PR. The documentation drift risk is low. No threat-model update is needed from this documentation alone.
